verdict.reasoning: Patient reports waking with a “really horrible pain on the left side of my head… a real kind of headachy feeling” that woke him “around, five thirty ish” and is still present.
Headache persists (“Is the headache still present now? – Yes, it is.”) and is unilateral/left-sided (“really horrible pain on the left side of my head… more prominent on the left side”).

When asked about bright lights, patient says “I'm a little bit sensitive it just, it kind of, makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle,” consistent with mild photophobia.
Patient reports “When I first got up this morning, my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of subsided now, and I, seems to, be fine,” indicating initial dizziness that has resolved.

No neck stiffness (“do you have any neck stiffness…? – Uh, no.”), no fever (“do you have any fever? – No.”), and effectively no nausea/vomiting (“can I just double-check, are you feeling nauseous at all? – Um, not really…” and no vomiting mentioned).

Regarding lying down: “it kind of feels a little bit sore at first… so yeah, at the beginning it does, but then again that's just kind of, um, soothes a little bit… would you say ultimately, it's better when you lie down? – Uh, yeah, I would say so,” showing improvement after settling when lying down.
“In terms of… headache since this morning, have you taken anything for it yet? – I've taken some Paracetamol… Has that helped? – Um, not really, no.”
“I've had, um, so I had, like anxiety for about, two years now, and I've been on, uh, Sertraline for, a while.”
“Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure? – No.” and never having BP checked supports no known history of hypertension.
“I've been on, uh, Sertraline for, a while.” and later “Are you taking Sertraline at the moment? – Yes.”
“In terms of… headache since this morning… – I've taken some Paracetamol… No that's it, just Paracetamol.”
“Do you have any allergies to any medication? – Not that I'm aware of, no.”
“does anyone in your family have any migraines…? – Uh, no. They haven't.”
“are there any illnesses in your family? – … my mum's had a history of anxiety as well but, no kind of like physical illnesses…”

Work is stressful: “work's kind of, um, a bit stressful… I've got a lot going on… I've kind of, been, doing a lot of late nights.” Duration: “how long has that been the case for? – for probably about a couple of months now.”
“are you living by yourself… or living with someone else? – Um, I live with my partner.”
“Are you a smoker? – No.”
“how much exercise would you do normally a week? – so normally I, try to go running at least three times a week.”
Diet: “what's your diet like? – Um, it's OK, um, it's nothing, it's nothing um, really healthy, um, but it's fine. … I wouldn't say unhealthy.” summarised as ‘OK’.
“do you have any pets at home? – Uh, I have a cat.”

Doctor: “it sounds like it might be one of two things… tension headache… The other possibility is, um, migraine as well,” and headache is described as “more prominent on the left side,” i.e., acute unilateral left-sided with migraine vs tension-type differential.

Severe, woke from sleep (“really horrible pain… it woke me up… around, five thirty ish”), mild photophobia (“a little bit sensitive” to bright lights), and explicitly no fever, neck stiffness, or significant nausea/vomiting as previously quoted.
“I've taken some Paracetamol… Has that helped? – Um, not really, no,” indicating ineffectiveness.

Stress: ongoing work stress and late nights (“doing a lot of late nights”). Doctor: “maybe look, explore things to try and decrease the stress from work… sometimes dehydration and you know uh, fatigue can be causes of headaches as well,” and recommends 7–8 hours sleep, implying sleep deprivation/stress as contributors.
History of anxiety and on sertraline are both explicitly stated: “I had, like anxiety for about, two years now, and I've been on, uh, Sertraline… Are you taking Sertraline at the moment? – Yes.”
Work-related stress: “work's kind of, um, a bit stressful at the moment. I've got a lot going on… backlog of work… doing a lot of late nights.”
Doctor asks about self-harm: “Do you have any… thoughts about harming yourself or hurting yourself? – No.” Equivalent to denial of suicidal ideation.
“the things that we'd start off first line, if someone had migraine… would be to start Ibuprofen… that's one thing we can start.”
“You can keep on taking Paracetamol as well if you like, but the, the Ibuprofen's um, actually more effective.”
“there'll be a summary of all of this in the notes. And I'll also leave a link, to some of the danger signs of symptoms of headaches, in the notes. If you can read through that in your own time…”
“maybe consider taking some time off work… maybe having a week off if you self-certify, that might help with things.”
“I'd also like you to explore, counselling options as well so there's, a counselling service in your area, that I can give you the link for, for you to self-refer.”
“ensure that you're having a minimum of seven, eight hours sleep at night, every night.”
“you're drinking a minimum of, um, one point five to two litres uh, of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea.”
“what, we're gonna do is, we'll have a follow-up in a week's time… So we'll, we'll touch base in a week's time…”
“if we're finding that things are not getting better, we might need to arrange some blood tests or um, look at uh, other possibilities…”

“if anything changes in the meantime, or you get worried or things get worse. Feel free, have a lower threshold for ringing us back and we can book you an appointment, and we can reassess the situation.”
